project.name: LipatDorm
project.title: LipatDorm: A Budget-Friendly Micro-Moving and Cargo-Sharing Platform for Dormitory Students and Renters
project.purpose: Create a modern, responsive landing page prototype for LipatDorm. The website should demonstrate how the system helps dormitory students and renters move their belongings at a lower cost while promoting responsible consumption and reuse under SDG 12.
project.design_goal:
The landing page MUST be divided into separate full-screen sections. Each section should represent one major feature or concept of the system.
Use vertical snap scrolling so that scrolling moves naturally from one section to the next.
Each section should feel like a separate presentation slide while still being part of one continuous website.

scroll_behavior.section_behavior: Each section should use approximately 100vh height. Each section should have: - scroll-snap-align: start - responsive layout - smooth entrance animation - content reveal animation
scroll_behavior.navigation:
Add vertical navigation dots on the right side of the screen. Each dot represents one section.
The active dot must change when the user reaches another section.
Clicking a navigation dot should smoothly scroll to its section.
scroll_behavior.section_counter:
Display a small section counter such as:
01 / 21 02 / 21 03 / 21
Update the number based on the currently visible section.

visual_style.target_audience: Dormitory students, renters, local drivers, vehicle owners, buyers, sellers, and people interested in sustainable reuse.

section.name: Hero / Opening
section.headline: MOVE SMART. SPEND LESS. WASTE LESS.
section.description: LipatDorm is a budget-friendly micro-moving and cargo-sharing platform designed for dormitory students and renters.
section.visual: Show a dormitory environment with: - small pickup / multicab - boxes - electric fan - mattress - study table - plastic drawers - route/map elements - floating booking cards

section.name: The Problem
section.headline: MOVING SHOULD NOT BE THIS EXPENSIVE.

card.title: Expensive
card.description: Large moving trucks can be too expensive for short-distance dormitory moves.

card.title: Inefficient
card.description: Students may need multiple trips using small vehicles.

card.title: Wasteful
card.description: Students may abandon or throw away usable furniture and appliances because transporting them is difficult.

section.name: The LipatDorm Solution
section.headline: ONE PLATFORM. A SMARTER WAY TO MOVE.

feature.title: Right-Sized Rides
feature.description: Match cargo with appropriately sized local vehicles.

feature.title: Cargo-Sharing
feature.description: Students moving in similar directions can share one trip and split the cost.

feature.title: Pass-It-On
feature.description: Give usable furniture and appliances another owner instead of throwing them away.

section.name: Right-Sized Rides
section.headline: THE RIGHT VEHICLE FOR THE RIGHT CARGO.
section.description: LipatDorm connects students with local owners of suitable small vehicles such as multicabs, small pickups, and utility vans.
section.visual: Show different cargo sizes being matched with appropriate vehicles.

section.name: Smart Booking
section.headline: BOOK YOUR MOVE IN A FEW SIMPLE STEPS.
section.visual: Show a realistic booking interface inside a floating phone or dashboard mockup.

section.name: Map & Route Coordination
section.headline: PLAN THE ROUTE. COORDINATE THE MOVE.
section.description: LipatDorm uses Leaflet.js to display pickup locations, destinations, drivers, shared cargo, and planned routes on an interactive map.
section.visual: Display a large interactive Leaflet.js map. Show a sample pickup point, destination, driver position, and route between locations.

section.name: Sample Route Test
section.headline: TEST A LIPATDORM ROUTE.
section.description: Demonstrate how LipatDorm calculates and visualizes a sample moving route using Leaflet.js and a routing service.

sample_route.pickup: WMSU Main Campus / Nearby Student Dorm Area

test_sequence.step: Calculate or load the road route
Draw the route on the map
Animate the driver along the route

section.status_sequence: READY ROUTE CALCULATED DRIVER ASSIGNED DRIVER EN ROUTE ARRIVED AT PICKUP CARGO LOADED IN TRANSIT ARRIVED

section.name: Transparent Pricing
section.headline: NO SURPRISE PRICES.

section.name: Split the Cost

section.name: Pass-It-On
section.headline: DON'T THROW IT AWAY. PASS IT ON.
section.description: Students can list usable furniture, appliances, and other dormitory items for sale, donation, or free claiming.

leaflet_requirements.routing: Use OSRM or another suitable routing service for the prototype.
leaflet_requirements.important:
Leaflet.js is responsible for displaying the interactive map, markers, routes, and map interface.
Leaflet.js itself does not calculate road routes. A routing service should be used when actual road routing is required.
leaflet_requirements.route_demo: Include a working sample route test in Section 07.

animations.scroll_reveal: Elements should animate into view when their section becomes active.
animations.map_animation: Driver marker can move along the sample route during the route test.
animations.cards: Cards should slightly translate or fade into view.
animations.counters: SDG impact numbers should animate when Section 19 becomes visible.
animations.parallax: Use subtle parallax effects where appropriate. Do not make animations excessive or distracting.

responsive_design.desktop: Use large layouts with multiple cards and large map visualizations.
responsive_design.mobile: Stack content vertically. Keep buttons accessible. Keep the map usable. Keep text readable. Preserve the section-by-section snap experience.

technology.icons: Use an appropriate open icon library if necessary.

prototype_rules.rule: The page MUST be divided into 21 clearly identifiable sections.
Each section should occupy approximately one viewport height.
Use vertical snap scrolling between sections.
Do not combine all features into one long section.
Each section should focus on one major LipatDorm feature.
Make the prototype look like a real startup/product website, not a simple school HTML page.
Keep the design clean, modern, professional, and student-friendly.
All buttons and navigation elements should have visible interaction feedback.
Use sample/demo data where backend functionality is not available.
Clearly label estimated environmental impact values as estimates.

project.final_experience:
The user should feel like they are scrolling through an interactive presentation of the complete LipatDorm system.
Every section should introduce one idea:
Problem → Solution → Right-Sized Vehicles → Booking → Leaflet Map → Route Test → Pricing → Cargo Sharing → Cost Sharing → Pass-It-On → Marketplace → Reuse → Smart Matching → Tracking → Safety → Complete Journey → SDG 12 Impact → App Preview → Final Call to Action
